focus.title: 欧盟碳边境调节机制过渡期临近，中国出口企业需加快碳数据合规布局
focus.summary: 欧盟碳边境调节机制（CBAM）过渡期将于2026年底结束，2027年起进入正式征收阶段。涉及钢铁、铝、水泥、化肥、电力和氢能等六大行业。中国出口企业需建立产品碳足迹核算体系，收集并验证嵌入碳排放数据，否则将面临额外成本。建议企业尽快梳理对欧出口产品清单，与欧盟进口商确认数据申报要求，并探索使用绿电、低碳工艺降低碳强度。同时关注欧盟认可的中国碳市场衔接可能性。
focus.source: 来源：欧盟委员会气候行动总司 · 2026.10.02
focus.title_en: EU CBAM Transition Period Nears End: Chinese Exporters Urged to Accelerate Carbon Data Compliance
focus.summary_en: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) transition period will conclude by the end of 2026, with the definitive regime applying from 2027 to six sectors: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity, and hydrogen. Chinese exporters must establish product carbon footprint accounting systems, collect and verify embedded emissions data, or face additional costs. Companies should promptly map EU-bound products, confirm data reporting requirements with EU importers, and explore green electricity and low-carbon processes to reduce carbon intensity. Attention should also be paid to the potential linkage with China's carbon market.

case.title: 新加坡上诉法院明确跨境仲裁中第三方资助的披露义务与利益冲突审查标准
case.summary: 新加坡上诉法院近期在一宗涉及中国企业的国际仲裁裁决执行案中，明确了第三方资助（TPF）的披露义务范围，并指出资助方与仲裁员之间的间接利益关系可能构成撤销裁决的理由。该案涉及一家中国工程公司在新加坡仲裁后申请执行裁决，被申请人以资助方与首席仲裁员存在业务往来为由请求撤销。法院认为，若资助协议中的利益安排可能影响仲裁员公正性，当事人有义务主动披露。此案提示中国企业在选择资助方时需进行利益冲突尽调，并在仲裁程序中及时披露资助安排。
case.source: 来源：新加坡上诉法院 · 2026年9月
case.title_en: Singapore Court of Appeal Clarifies Disclosure Duties and Conflict Review Standards for Third-Party Funding in Cross-Border Arbitration
case.summary_en: The Singapore Court of Appeal recently clarified the scope of disclosure obligations for third-party funding (TPF) in an enforcement case involving a Chinese enterprise, holding that indirect interests between a funder and an arbitrator may justify setting aside an award. The case arose when a Chinese engineering company sought to enforce an award in Singapore, and the respondent challenged it based on business ties between the funder and the presiding arbitrator. The court held that parties must proactively disclose funding arrangements if they could affect arbitrator impartiality. This underscores the need for Chinese companies to conduct conflict due diligence on funders and promptly disclose TPF arrangements.
case.source_en: Source: Singapore Court of Appeal · September 2026

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区推出跨境商事纠纷“一站式”在线解纷平台，强化涉外法律服务
policy.summary: 粤港澳大湾区近期上线跨境商事纠纷“一站式”在线解纷平台，整合粤港澳三地调解、仲裁和诉讼资源，为跨境企业提供在线立案、调解、仲裁和司法确认服务。平台支持中英葡三语，并引入香港、澳门调解机构和仲裁机构。此举旨在降低跨境解纷成本，提升大湾区法治化营商环境。企业可通过平台在线提交纠纷材料，选择适用香港、澳门或内地法律，并实现裁决的跨境认可与执行。建议出海企业熟悉平台流程，在合同中约定适用该平台解纷。
policy.source: 来源：广东省司法厅 · 2026年9月
policy.title_en: Greater Bay Area Launches One-Stop Online Dispute Resolution Platform for Cross-Border Commercial Disputes
policy.summary_en: The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area recently launched a one-stop online dispute resolution platform integrating mediation, arbitration, and litigation resources across the three jurisdictions. The platform offers online case filing, mediation, arbitration, and judicial confirmation services in Chinese, English, and Portuguese, and includes mediation and arbitration institutions from Hong Kong and Macao. It aims to reduce cross-border dispute resolution costs and enhance the rule-of-law business environment. Companies can submit disputes online, choose applicable law, and seek cross-border recognition and enforcement of awards. Export-oriented enterprises should familiarise themselves with the platform and consider designating it in contracts.
policy.source_en: Source: Guangdong Provincial Department of Justice · September 2026

analysis.title: 秦林蒿律师：美国对华半导体出口管制新规下，企业需构建“穿透式”合规体系
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师研判：美国近期进一步收紧对华半导体出口管制，将更多中国实体列入实体清单，并扩大外国直接产品规则适用范围。中国企业面临供应链断供、次级制裁及高管刑事责任等多重风险。建议企业立即开展供应链穿透排查，识别受控物项和交易对手；建立出口管制合规内控机制，包括最终用户和最终用途审查；在合同中加入合规陈述与保证、终止权条款；对敏感交易进行法律意见书论证。同时，关注中国《反外国制裁法》下的阻断与反制措施，平衡合规与业务连续性。
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin: Under New U.S. Semiconductor Export Controls, Companies Need a 'Look-Through' Compliance System
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's view: The U.S. recently tightened semiconductor export controls on China, adding more Chinese entities to the Entity List and expanding the foreign direct product rule. Chinese companies face supply chain disruptions, secondary sanctions, and potential executive criminal liability. Companies should immediately conduct look-through supply chain audits to identify controlled items and counterparties; establish export control compliance programs including end-user and end-use checks; incorporate compliance representations, warranties, and termination rights in contracts; and obtain legal opinions for sensitive transactions. Meanwhile, monitor blocking and countermeasures under China's Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law to balance compliance and business continuity.
